 Watch Sunderland vs Leeds United for free from anywhere as the Black Cats look to end their four-match losing run in the Premier League against Daniel Farke's side. FourFourTwo has all the details on live streams and TV channels, wherever you are in the world.
 Sunderland vs Leeds United: key information 
 Kick-off time: 4:30pm GMT / 12:30pm ET / 2:30am AEDT (Mon)
 FREE Stream: USA Network via YouTube TV's 5-day free trial (US)
 TV & Streaming: Sky Sports (UK) / Stan Sport (AUS)
 Watch from anywhere: Use Proton VPN to unblock your stream

 The visitors will aim to capitalise on the Black Cats' tight turnaround, with Farke's team in decent form after losing just one of their opening seven Premier League games.

 View Deal Sunderland vs Leeds United: Preview 
 The Premier League table does not look pretty for Sunderland, but when you dig a little deeper it becomes clear why the Black Cats are bottom of the pile.
 Regis Le Bris' men have had a tough set of fixtures to start the campaign, including games against Manchester City, Arsenal and Brighton & Hove Albion, while they have also had to contend with the Thursday-Sunday slog of Europa League football.
 Their results on the continent have been considerably better than at home, with Thursday's 1-1 draw away to Polish champions Lech Poznan the first time they have dropped points in the Europa League this season.
 The Black Cats have lost their last four Premier League games and taken just four points overall, but they could be boosted by the return from injury of striker Brian Brobbey against Leeds United. Defender Kevin Danso is suspended, though, having been sent off in the defeat at Bournemouth last Sunday.
 SEE ALSO How to watch Premier League 2026/27: TV Guide, Streams & Fixtures 
 While Sunderland have won just once in the league this season, Leeds arrive at the Stadium of Light with only one defeat to their name — away to champions Arsenal a fortnight ago.
 Daniel Farke's side were then held 1-1 by rivals Manchester United last weekend, their fourth draw in their opening seven league matches, and the Whites boss will see this as an excellent chance to return to winning ways.
 Leeds have had a free midweek so should be much fresher than their opponents, which could see Farke name an unchanged starting line-up for the sixth successive Premier League game.
 They remain without injured defender Joe Rodon, while winger Dan James has sat out the last two matches with a back issue.
 FourFourTwo's prediction 
 Sunderland 1-2 Leeds United 
 The tight turnaround between their trip to Poland and this game could cost the Black Cats.
